title: Quest 3/3S: pin device profiles to the Quest 2 baseline and document supported headsets (P-31)
acceptance: Meta_Quest_3 and Meta_Quest_3S device profiles apply the same rendering settings as Oculus_Quest2
An automation test loads the device profiles and checks the pinned values
docs/TOOLCHAIN.md lists the supported headsets, controllers and refresh rate
description: From ADR-0003. The engine's Quest 2 profile sets sg.ShadowQuality=1 but its Quest 3/3S profiles do not, so without project profiles Quest 3 would render differently from Quest 2. No Quest-3-only quality increase in this task.

history.note: Approved by the owner in chat on 2026-11-17 (Approve T-0046). Recorded on the owner's behalf by claude-code-dartonx-pc.

result.summary: Quest 3 and 3S now get exactly the Quest 2 rendering settings. Config/DefaultDeviceProfiles.ini adds sg.ShadowQuality=1 to Meta_Quest_3 and Meta_Quest_3S (the engine gave them 2 via Android_OpenXR while Quest 2 has 1). New test ETM.Platform.DeviceProfiles.Quest3MatchesQuest2 resolves each profile's full inherited settings and requires Quest 3 and 3S to match Quest 2 in both directions. docs/TOOLCHAIN.md has a Supported headsets section (profiles, Touch Plus via the Touch profile, 72 Hz, verification status). The manifest already listed quest3 and quest3s, so it was not changed.
result.verification: Built on UE 5.8.4, zero errors and warnings; all 44 ETM tests pass. Ran the new test with DefaultDeviceProfiles.ini removed: it fails with 'Meta_Quest_3 sets sg.shadowquality=1 like Quest 2 (has 2)', so it detects the mismatch. Editor only; no Quest 3 or 3S has run the game.
result.remaining: Device check on a real Quest 3 or 3S is T-0047 and needs a headset (the build PC has only a Quest 2). Touch Plus through the Touch profile is expected, not seen. Quest 3 renders at its higher recommended resolution: measure before raising any other setting. Quest Pro stays in the manifest until T-0041 decides.
